A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable main text, algorithms, equations, and complete appendices. v1 Appendices A–D correspond to v2 Appendices B–E; v2 adds an illustrative Appendix A.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical algorithms, convergence bounds, and proofs, but reports no original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Appendix A gives closed-form calculations for a Tiger POMDP example; no experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes reward generation from sampling R(r|s,a) before the transition to obtaining R(s,a,s') after sampling the successor state. The linear critics, temporal-difference updates, and natural actor-critic update procedure otherwise remain the same.

E1.justification: Neither version reports datasets or environments used in training or empirical evaluation. The added Tiger POMDP is an analytical illustration, not an additional evaluated benchmark.

E2.justification: Cayci et al.'s symmetric natural actor-critic remains the theoretical comparator. Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons; newly cited methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to concentrability and theorem parameters concern the mathematical analysis, while the added sampling explanation documents the existing sampling requirement.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies. The new aliasing example is a mathematical counterexample rather than a supplementary experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's suggestion to investigate critic-error variance is future work, not new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No measured performance values, rankings, or empirical result entries are reported in either version. v2's added closed-form Tiger values and revised convergence guarantees are theoretical changes covered under T1.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 replaces v1's expected agent-state/action occupancy ratio with a supremum over state–agent-state–action triples, strengthening the concentrability assumption. Theorem 5 now sets asymmetric inference error to zero, supported by a separate Markov performance-difference argument in Appendix E; v1 applied the POMDP bound to both settings. v2 also adds the analytical Tiger counterexample and revises mathematical details, including the m-step contraction factor and distribution-shift derivation.

C1.justification: The central theoretical justification is retained. The abstract and introduction now claim elimination of multiple aliasing-related error terms, reflecting the added inference-error distinction. The conclusion narrows 'insensitive to aliasing' to 'less sensitive to aliasing.'

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly acknowledges that asymmetric advantage regression can have a larger residual error, even in the tabular case, qualifying the benefit of reduced critic aliasing. v2 also discusses the expectation-only nature of the bounds, explains concentrability requirements, and adds nonlinear recurrent approximation as a future direction.

D1.justification: Section 3 adds instructions for obtaining discounted-visitation samples using a geometrically sampled rollout length with parameter 1−γ. This supplies an implementation explanation for the existing sampling requirement. Neither version supplies code, hardware specifications, or experimental implementation details.

R1.justification: v2 adds a focused comparison with Cai et al. (2024), distinguishing its model-based PAC analysis from this paper's model-free expectation bounds and symmetric comparison. It also adds Kaelbling et al. (1998), Kakade and Langford (2002), and Schulman et al. (2015), and removes Hafner et al. (2019).

P1.justification: v2 consistently replaces 'finite state policy' with 'agent-state policy,' expands background explanations and section roadmaps, edits prose, and adds an Impact Statement. The main section sequence remains intact; existing proof appendices are renumbered after the new example.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 1, showing the Tiger example's states, observations, actions, and rewards. Algorithm boxes shift within the columns, and some theorem equations are reformatted. The overall two-column main text and single-column appendix layout remain.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the qualification of v1's broad aliasing-benefit interpretation by acknowledging larger gradient residuals and narrowing the conclusion. The worked example and sampling instructions improve checkability. Gains are limited: Theorem 5 now requires stronger concentrability, and Appendix E's final Eq. (284) still expands the inference term generically despite the new asymmetric zero-error case.
